ecology.note: Seven assumed settings, two seeds, with and without a neighbour cue. Every run stops at the edge of a reused aerodynamic domain. That is a domain stop, not a landing, an escape, or a biological outcome.

mission.label: Molecular
mission.open: One molecule-to-fin source is indexed: Daane et al. 2021 shows a lat4a x kcnh2a interaction that phenocopies flying-fish fin proportion in zebrafish, with genome-wide association signatures across 35 species. The flying-fish side is association, not demonstration, and transfer to a halfbeak is an unestablished hypothesis. No parameter links it to wing area or loading.
mission.coupling: No executable coupling to macromolecular structure or to fin geometry.

mission.label: Macromolecular
mission.open: No structure or binding-affinity input for any fin-patterning protein. The stopped KCNE1 protocol shows what happens when a structure covers only 20.27% of an assay: the test is stopped, not run.
mission.coupling: No executable coupling to subcellular organisation.

mission.label: Subcellular
mission.open: Nothing indexed. Newer molecule-to-fin evidence (Daane 2021) is reported available but not yet in this snapshot.
mission.coupling: No executable coupling to cell behaviour.

mission.label: Cellular
mission.open: Daane et al. 2021 describes bioelectric and amino-acid-transport signalling that affects fin proportion in zebrafish; no exocoetid cell-level measurement is indexed. The bridge to exocoetid fins is unestablished.
mission.coupling: No executable coupling to tissue mechanics or patterning.

mission.label: Tissue
mission.open: Davenport (1992, abstract only) reports flying fish carry no more red axial muscle than a cruising mackerel, and that take-off acceleration probably needs anaerobic white muscle. No muscle power parameter enters any model here.
mission.coupling: No executable coupling from muscle tissue to launch speed.

mission.label: Organ
mission.open: Fin morphometrics are measured (pectoral fins supply 76-92% of wing area; hypocaudal lobe is 63.1 +/- 0.5% of caudal area). Only empirical allometry links fin size to mass; there is no model of how a fin forms or what loads it can bear.
mission.coupling: Empirical allometry only (Fish 1990 fits). Not a mechanistic coupling.

mission.label: Neural / control
mission.open: No source on taxiing, take-off or glide control is indexed. Whether a candidate can be stabilised by control rather than by geometry is an open question.
mission.coupling: No executable coupling to flight dynamics.

mission.label: Organism
mission.open: Wing loading, aspect ratio, glide distance and ground effect are measured or computed in the literature. Maximum L/D = 11.0 is a 1929 calculation relayed by Fish, not a measurement. Davenport 2003 (the maximum-size stability argument) has not been read.
mission.coupling: The browser calculation below is the only runnable organism-scale model; it is arithmetic on published fits, not a flight simulation.

mission.label: Developmental
mission.open: Juveniles under 0.05 m do not fly and their paired fins are hypothesised to be flotation organs (Hubbs 1933, relayed by Fish). How fin proportions emerge during growth is not modelled. The seeded Turing records are about pattern formation in general, not about fins.
mission.coupling: No executable coupling from developmental programme to adult morphometry.

mission.label: Collective
mission.open: Nothing indexed on schooling or group launch.

mission.label: Ecological / evolutionary
mission.open: The predator-escape hypothesis is Darwin's (1859) and, as far as the report's search reaches, has never been quantified, so it is not used as a constraint. Extant exocoetids stop at 50 cm total length (69 FishBase species with a parsed maximum), which is an observation about extant species and not a physical limit. The only exocoetid genome assembly is scaffold-level (GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger); no comparative exocoetid genomics is supportable.
mission.coupling: Reachability from a beloniform ancestor is NOT established by any check on this page. The developmental and evolutionary bridge to the organism scale is an open question.

erk.note: Simulated Erk trigger wave on one regenerating zebrafish scale (Hayden 2021 parameters; growth form assumed). Not a flying-fish scale and not a microscope image.

limits: Launch prototypes from Frontier. Nothing here has been printed, weighed, glided, or thrown. The picture is the revision’s STL parts, moved by each part’s print-to-fish transform. It is not a living fish.
